title: Light stars and paths in planar graphs of minimum degree five (Jendrol'–Madaras)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of Jendrol' and Madaras (1996), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. Every planar graph of minimum degree at least five has: a vertex X of degree five with three distinct neighbours A1, A2, A3 such that deg A1 = 5, deg A2 ≤ 6 and deg A3 ≤ 7, or deg A1 = deg A2 = deg A3 = 6 (light_star, Theorem 1; in particular a 5-vertex with three neighbours of degree at most seven, "Lebesgue's star"); a vertex of degree five with four distinct neighbours of degree at most ten (light_star4, Theorem 2); and a path on four vertices whose degrees sum to at most 23 (light_path4, Theorem 3). Three statements. The proofs are discharging arguments run on the rotation system with face charges instead of triangulating or using edge-maximal counterexamples; the local analyses (32768, 16384, 32768 and 100000 configurations) and the parity of an 11-cycle are checked by decide in the kernel.
